title: Define call/identity/promise state enums + transition tables
description:
WHY: v1 compressed everything into one 4-state machine, mixing identity, dialogue progress, and
outcomes. The Codex critique (adopted) split them: three orthogonal machines, ALL transitions
performed by application code — LLM output is only ever a proposal. This is the load-bearing
architecture: 'CONFIRMED is an authorization fact, not an LLM label.'
WHAT (exact tables, implement verbatim):
CALL: IDLE->PREFLIGHT->READY->CONNECTING->ACTIVE->COMPLETED; PREFLIGHT->BLOCKED;
CONNECTING/ACTIVE->DEGRADED; ACTIVE/DEGRADED->OPERATOR_TAKEOVER;
ACTIVE/DEGRADED/OPERATOR_TAKEOVER->ENDED.
IDENTITY: UNVERIFIED->VERIFYING->CONFIRMED; UNVERIFIED/VERIFYING->THIRD_PARTY;
CONFIRMED->UNVERIFIED (explicit handover or identity uncertainty); CONFIRMED->THIRD_PARTY (new
speaker identifies as another person). Identity ALWAYS starts UNVERIFIED per call — never restored
from a previous call.
PROMISE: NONE->CANDIDATE->READ_BACK->CONFIRMED->COMMITTED; CANDIDATE/READ_BACK->CORRECTED->
READ_BACK (corrections force re-read-back); CANDIDATE/READ_BACK/CORRECTED->ABANDONED.
ACCEPTANCE: single module of enums + a transition-validity function; illegal transition raises a
typed error and writes an event; unit-testable without any I/O.
close_reason: Defined immutable StrEnum contracts and exact legal transition tables for call (13 edges), identity (7 edges including V2 THIRD_PARTY->VERIFYING amendment), and promise (10 edges). Added pure validation, typed InvalidStateTransition with append-ready rejection evidence, stable JSON rendering, and unconditional fresh-call initial states. Focused Ruff/format passed; 12 state contract tests passed; full concurrent suite 19 passed.

title: Define typed LLM action schema + per-state validation rules
description:
WHY: Model prose must never directly trigger a database write. The LLM proposes a typed action;
code validates it against the current state before anything happens.
WHAT: JSON schema — {intent: offer_promise|correct_promise|confirm|deny|handover|request_human|
other, amount_minor: int|null, date_phrase: str|null, response_draft: str}. Validation rules:
amount/date fields REJECTED unless identity is CONFIRMED; 'confirm' only meaningful in promise
state READ_BACK; 'handover' valid in any active state (triggers demotion); unknown fields dropped;
malformed JSON => treated as 'other' with a clarification template, never a crash.
Pre-CONFIRMED the LLM's ONLY job is intent classification for template selection (see template
bank bead) — its draft text is discarded, never spoken.
ACCEPTANCE: schema file + validator function with unit tests covering: valid post-CONFIRMED offer;
amount field while UNVERIFIED (rejected); malformed JSON (safe fallback); handover intent (state
demotion signal emitted).
close_reason: Implemented typed LLM action schema and deterministic per-state validator: malformed payloads fail to safe clarification, unknown fields are dropped, pre-confirm private fields/drafts and write-capable intents are rejected, confirm requires READ_BACK, and active-call handover emits an explicit demotion signal. Added 7 focused tests; full backend gates passed (31 tests) and frontend check passed.

title: Define tool permission matrix (7 tools x states x conditions)
description:
WHY: 'Tools physically unavailable' is the demo's central claim; the matrix is its written law.
WHAT (implement verbatim):
submit_verification -> VERIFYING only; two-attempt limit.
read_mock_account -> CONFIRMED only; active call.
create_promise_candidate -> CONFIRMED only; positive amount, future/allowed date.
correct_promise_candidate -> CONFIRMED only; existing uncommitted candidate.
commit_promise -> CONFIRMED only; candidate read back AND explicit yes recorded.
schedule_content_free_callback -> THIRD_PARTY only; payload contains NO account fields.
end_call -> any active state; requires valid end reason.
Disallowed calls return a TYPED failure, write a tool_decision event (tool, allowed=false, states,
reason), and mutate nothing — no partial writes.
ACCEPTANCE: matrix encoded as data (not if-chains) so the WATCH column and the test runner can
render/assert it; unit test per row for both the allowed and a denied case.
close_reason: Implemented declarative seven-tool permission matrix with orthogonal state gates, typed recorded denials, fail-closed technical-state locking, and 17 focused tests. Full backend gate: Ruff clean and 42 tests passed; frontend check/build green.

title: Promise engine: candidate -> read-back -> correction -> idempotent commit
description:
WHY: One ledger row cannot prove the invariant. The engine event-sources the promise so evidence
shows WHAT was parsed, that it was READ BACK, whether it was CORRECTED, and that an EXPLICIT yes
authorized the single commit. Also kills the lakh/hazaar mishear class: no number reaches the
ledger unconfirmed.
WHAT: parse amount into integer minor units (Rs 1,500 -> 150000 paise); normalize date phrase to
ISO in Asia/Kolkata against seeded demo time ('Friday' -> next Friday's date); REJECT past or
impossible dates; read back in dual format — digits + words + weekday + absolute date: 'Pandrah
sau rupaye — 1-5-0-0 — Friday, [generated date]. Sahi hai?'; accept only an explicit affirmative
classified in READ_BACK state; any correction updates the candidate (revision++) and FORCES
another read-back; commit exactly once via idempotency key; call ending pre-confirmation ->
ABANDONED, no promise row.
ACCEPTANCE: tests — 1500-commit; 1500->1050 correction commits only the revision after second
read-back; 'no' at read-back leaves no promise row; duplicate affirmative -> one row.

title: Break-glass takeover with strict safety ordering
description:
WHY: When the operator takes over, two speakers or stale model output acting concurrently is the
disaster case. The ORDER is the feature (Codex spec, adopted verbatim).
WHAT — on Takeover click, strictly: (1) revoke agent tool access; (2) cancel pending LLM/TTS
work; (3) stop TTS playback; (4) write OPERATOR_TAKEOVER event; (5) ONLY THEN open Priya's mic
path. The agent CANNOT resume after takeover in the MVP; Priya ends the call with a required
reason -> ENDED_OPERATOR. Stale async results arriving after step 2 are dropped (call-state check
in every callback).

work logged, disposition ENDED_OPERATOR with reason; manual rehearsal includes one live takeover.
close_reason: Implemented strict break-glass ordering and operator flow: synchronous authority revoke -> pending LLM/TTS/STT cancellation -> generated/browser speech stop before the first persistence await; persisted OPERATOR_TAKEOVER; permanent generation/state callback gate; idempotent duplicate takeover; required bounded reason and ENDED_OPERATOR-only terminal boundary; mounted /api/takeover and /api/call/end; persistent operator banner with takeover disabled and only reason-gated End remaining. Evidence: 13 focused tests including mid-LLM cancellation, stubborn stale callback, safety-effect failure, persistence failure, API contracts, and disposition; full backend Ruff/format + 404 tests; frontend 5 unit tests, svelte-check, and production build. Live controller registration is the explicit sarvam-4ae integration seam; physical rehearsal remains tracked by dependent sarvam-ztt.

title: Promise state mutates before append-only evidence is durable
description:
Closed-bead audit finding against sarvam-bb8 and the evidence claims in sarvam-bfo/sarvam-vmo.

`PromiseEngine` persists candidate/read-back/confirmation/commit state, applies in-memory state, and only then calls the separate event recorder (`backend/app/promise.py` committed HEAD lines 718-870). These are independent autocommit transactions. An evidence write failure therefore leaves domain rows/state without the append-only event chain that is supposed to prove them.

Deterministic in-memory reproduction (2026-07-26): inject `record_event` that raises. `create_candidate` raises to its caller but leaves engine state CANDIDATE and a persisted `promise_candidates` row `(call-audit-promise-evidence-promise, revision 1, amount_minor 150000)` with zero promise events. The same ordering exists for read-back, confirmation, and commit; a failure after promise insertion can create a business row without PROMISE_COMMITTED evidence/disposition.

Required fix: each promise transition must persist its domain mutation and corresponding monotonic evidence atomically, or roll back both. In-memory state advances only after the transaction commits. Retrying the same operation must be idempotent and reconstructable from SQLite after interruption. Commit and final disposition need an explicitly defined atomic or fail-closed ordering so ENDED_TECHNICAL cannot coexist with an unproven promise row.

Required tests: failure injection at every repository/event boundary for create, correction, read-back, explicit confirmation, commit, duplicate suppression, and abandonment; assert zero partial rows/state/events after failure; restart/replay reconstruction; controller-level forced persistence failure; full matrix and runner diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Candidate/correction/read-back/confirmation/commit/abandonment mutations and their corresponding evidence rows commit atomically or both roll back.
2. In-memory promise state advances only after durable success and can be reconstructed from SQLite after interruption.
3. Failure injection at every persistence/evidence boundary leaves zero partial rows, state, or orphan evidence.
4. Promise commit and terminal disposition ordering prevents an unproven promise row from coexisting with ENDED_TECHNICAL or another non-business outcome.
5. Retries and duplicate affirmatives remain idempotent; the full matrix and evidence runner pass with detailed diagnostics.

Preserve the single sanctioned demo-reset path through an explicit scoped mechanism that cannot be reached during an active call and cannot affect non-demo rows. title: P0 DEMO-KILLER: orphaned ACTIVE call bricks the app after any backend restart
description:
REPRODUCED LIVE by the orchestrator at ~14:25 IST against the running backend. This can end the demo permanently mid-slot. It outranks every other open bug.

SYMPTOM — unrecoverable deadlock:
  /api/preflight  -> BLOCKED_POLICY ['active_session']   (DB says a call is active)
  /api/call/start -> 409 'A current READY preflight is required'
  /api/reset      -> 403 'Demo reset is unavailable during an active call'
  /api/call/end   -> 404 'Active call was not found.'    (in-memory registry is empty)
  /api/takeover   -> 404 'Active call was not found.'
Every recovery path is blocked. The app cannot start a call, cannot end the old one, and
cannot reset. Only manual sqlite surgery clears it.

ROOT CAUSE: call lifecycle state is split across two stores with no reconciliation.
  - durable: calls row with ended=NULL, disposition=NULL  (survives restart)
  - ephemeral: in-memory lifecycle/takeover registry      (lost on restart)
After ANY backend restart (crash, --reload, laptop sleep, someone re-running uvicorn) the
durable row still reads ACTIVE while the registry that /end and /takeover consult is empty.

ACTUAL DB EVIDENCE at time of filing:
  call-c886ba2d-57a8-48a8-b916-57925f1537da | case-rakesh-001 | started 07:58:29Z |
  ended=None | disposition=None | transport=streaming_pcm16_ws

WHY THIS IS A DEMO-KILLER, not a nitpick: the demo protocol requires reset-between-runs
(3x happy, 3x third-party per sarvam-ztt). Any restart or any call that does not reach a
disposition leaves the app bricked for every subsequent run, including the judged one.
It also silently blocks the capped-case refusal beat, because preflight fails on
active_session before it can fail on contact_cap.

REQUIRED FIX (startup reconciliation — small, and it IS the product's own principle):
1. On app startup, find every calls row with ended IS NULL and reconcile it: write
   disposition=ENDED_TECHNICAL with reason 'orphaned by process restart', set ended, and
   append the events row. Fail CLOSED — a call whose process died did not produce a
   business outcome. This is exactly the plan's rule that technical failure never becomes
   a business outcome.
2. Make /api/call/end and /api/takeover degrade honestly: if the durable row is ACTIVE but
   the registry has no entry, do NOT 404 into a dead end. Either reconcile-then-end, or
   return a typed error the operator UI can act on.
3. Reset should be permitted to clear an orphaned (registry-less) active call, since by
   definition no live call can be harmed.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Start a call, kill uvicorn, restart it: preflight returns READY (not active_session),
  the orphaned call shows ENDED_TECHNICAL in evidence, reset works.
- Normal in-process end/takeover behaviour is unchanged (do not weaken the same-turn
  takeover ordering).
- Add a regression test that simulates the restart by clearing the in-memory registry while
  leaving the durable row ACTIVE.

INTERIM WORKAROUND for anyone blocked right now (safe, demo data only):
  sqlite3 backend/vachan.db "update calls set ended=datetime('now'),
    disposition='ENDED_TECHNICAL' where ended is null;"
Then /api/reset works again. Do this before every rehearsal until the fix lands.

title: Caller audio suppressed by the agent floor is silently truncated, yielding incomplete actions
description:
RUNTIME-PROVEN, reproduced 4 consecutive times. Blocks the promise beat (PROMISE stays NONE).

MECHANISM (sharpened after run call-d650e215 - the earlier 'caller talks over the agent'
reading was incomplete and is superseded)

Saaras finalizes a segment MID-SENTENCE. That partial fragment fires a full controller turn,
the turn takes the agent floor, and the REMAINDER OF THE SAME CALLER SENTENCE is then
discarded as audio_suppressed:agent_floor. So one spoken sentence is split into an acted-upon
fragment plus a silently dropped tail. The caller never interrupted anyone.

WHY IT LANDS ON THE AMOUNT EVERY TIME - HINDI WORD ORDER
The promise sentence is:
    मैं | शुक्रवार तक | पंद्रह सौ रुपये | दे दूँगा।
    I   | by Friday   | 1500 rupees     | will give
The deadline PRECEDES the amount in natural Hindi. An early cut after 'मैं शुक्रवार तक'
yields a fragment carrying the date and NOT the amount, so the model emits a well-formed
offer_promise with date_phrase='Friday' and amount_minor=None, denied as
invalid_action_facts=missing_amount. An English sentence ('I will pay 1500 by Friday') would
lose the DATE instead - so this is not amount-specific, it is order-specific. Any
single-utterance action whose required fields are spread across the sentence is exposed.

EVIDENCE
- call-d650e215: CONFIRMED at seq 16, ledger then quiet 10s (agent NOT speaking) before the
  promise clip was fired. Still seq 20 audio_suppressed:agent_floor -> seq 21
  tool_denied:create_promise_candidate, tool_decisions.reason=invalid_action_facts=missing_amount.
  This run disproves the 'probe fired too early' theory: the floor was idle when the clip started.
- Same signature in call-dd08d9ae (seq 18-19), call-cd9540d6 (seq 19-20).
- call-cc222ad4: the REFERENCE clip was cut instead, so normalize_reference_last4 saw too few
  digits, submit_verification never ran, identity never left VERIFYING.
- Note only ONE AUDIO_SUPPRESSED row appears per window (deduped), so the ledger understates
  how much audio was dropped.

NOT BROKEN - each verified, do not re-investigate
model (offer_promise/150000/'Friday' 6 of 6 on the full sentence), validate_llm_action,
_validated_model_amount_minor(150000), amount_in_hindi_words(1500)='pandrah sau',
normalize_promise_date('Friday')=2026-07-31, the permission gate (ALLOWED for
ACTIVE/CONFIRMED/NONE with those facts), and the promise state machine itself (runner 17/17
including case 05 confirmed-1500-promise-commits-exactly-once and A1 borrower-promise-offer on
real STT).

THE REFUSAL IS CORRECT. Never infer, default or back-fill a missing amount or date. Fix the
truncation, not the denial.

FIX DIRECTIONS
1. Do not act on a fragment. Require an end-of-speech signal before dispatching a turn, or
   hold the floor open until the caller's utterance actually completes.
2. While the floor is held, BUFFER caller PCM and deliver it as a continuation of the same
   utterance instead of dropping it.
3. On a missing required field, ask for that field specifically ('पूरी रकम फिर बताइए') rather
   than a generic CLARIFY, so a cut turn is recoverable inside the call.
4. Record in the AUDIO_SUPPRESSED row that suppression interrupted an in-progress utterance,
   and stop deduping away the extent of what was dropped.

DIAGNOSABILITY: events.redacted_reason only carries 'tool_denied:<tool>'. The cause is in
tool_decisions.reason:
  select seq, tool, allowed, reason from tool_decisions where call_id='...' order by seq;
controller.py now also logs it at WARNING (invalid_action_facts ...).

title: CONVENTION: Devanagari font/tracking rules — do not reintroduce mangled Hindi
description:

Fixed in a116bef. Hindi was mangling on screen. If you touch CSS, templates, or any surface
that renders Hindi, these are now project rules and AGENTS.md carries them under

1. Every font stack that can hold Hindi MUST name a Devanagari face. --font-mono previously
   ended at 'monospace' (no Devanagari coverage), so ledger Hindi was shaped by a Latin-only
   font and matras collapsed into the base glyph. Latin mono faces stay FIRST so digits and
   state labels keep their monospace grid; Devanagari falls through per glyph. Use --font-deva.
